title: Bazel session slots
description: Schema-first contract of the concurrent Bazel sessions: a bounded set of numbered slots, each slot one persistent Bazel server with its own short output base and its own generated packages, all sharing one content-addressed cache (disk cache, repository cache, repository contents cache, optional remote cache). A session claims exactly one slot for the duration of one invocation, so concurrent invocations never meet in one Bazel server lock.

Policy.description: Authored numbers. `servers`: the bound on concurrently existing Bazel servers is derived from the host (memory above the host capacity floor times `memoryShareBasisPoints`, divided by `residentMegabytes`; cores divided by `coresPerServer`), never below `minimum` and never above `maximum`; `serviceMaximum` bounds the service slots of a host; `nestedExtra` slots are added for a session that starts inside a Bazel action (a nested invocation must never wait for the slot its own parent holds); `heapMegabytes` is the JVM heap of one server and `residentMegabytes` its estimated resident size (heap plus metaspace, threads and the client); `jvmArguments` make an idle server give its heap back to the operating system (periodic collection, bounded free ratios), so the idle time costs little memory on every platform, not only where the system compresses idle pages. `waiting`: a session that finds every slot claimed polls every `pollMilliseconds` behind the fair picker and reports every `progressMilliseconds`. `retention`: how many generated packages one slot keeps, how old they may get, and how long an unused output base may sit idle before it is garbage. `stop`: a server exits a few seconds after its pid file is removed, the collector waits at most `timeoutMilliseconds` for it. `leases`: names of the resources inside the repository lease directory; `restoreMaximumResources` bounds the hierarchical restore locks of one snapshot before it falls back to the exclusive root lock.

MemoryPolicy.description: The host capacity memory floor rule (`hostCapacity.memory` of the build policy): the floor is `floorBasisPoints` of host memory clamped to the two bounds; only memory above it may be committed.

ServerPlan.description: What the host affords: `slots` build slots (`s0`, `s1`, ...) of Bazel servers of `heapMegabytes` each, held only while a build cycle runs, and `services` service slots (`d0`, `d1`, ...) held by sessions that launch long-running watch/serve/dev tasks for their whole lifetime, each with its own queue and its own bound, so any number of dev servers up to that bound never block a build; a service slot's server exits after the idle time and costs memory only while it builds; `cpuPerServer` and `memoryPerServerMegabytes` are the local resources one server may hand its actions when no capacity grant bounds the invocation; `limit` names the binding constraint.

SlotState.description: What a slot remembers between sessions, written beside its output base while the session holds the claim: the key of the last selection (a warm server and package are reused for it), the keys of the selections it served before, newest first (a record only: its package holds the last selection alone), and the time of the last use in epoch milliseconds.

Inventory.description: What exists on disk: per slot directory its remembered state (when any), the modification times of its generated packages and whether an output base exists; `foreign` lists entries below the server or workspace directory that are not slots. Sizes (`bytes`, `outputBaseBytes`) are present only when measured under pressure; `temporary` tells that a package keeps a leftover capture folder.

Garbage.description: What the collector would remove: packages (slot and key), output bases (slot, each stopped before removal), leftover capture folders of kept packages (slot and key), foreign entries of the server directory (stopped, removed) and foreign package directories. Under pressure (free bytes of the products image below the soft threshold) the oldest unprotected packages and then the longest idle output bases go until the target free space is reached.

Messages.description: Progress and status lines in English and German; `{name}` placeholders are replaced by the reported values.

en.waiting: [bazel] all {slots} Bazel server slots are in use; waiting for one ({seconds} s)
en.waiting-service: [bazel] all {slots} Bazel service slots are in use; waiting for one ({seconds} s)
en.warm: warm server and package for this selection
en.switch: the package of the slot is replaced in place for a different selection, the server stays
en.status-header: slot  state   last selection    last used
en.reaped: [bazel] stopped the idle Bazel server of slot {slot}: {live} servers would run and this host affords {budget}
en.reap-failed: [bazel] the idle server of slot {slot} did not stop ({reason}); its idle exit will end it
en.grown: [bazel] every base Bazel server slot is in use and {spare} MB of memory are idle: opening the extra slot {slot}
en.pressure: [bazel] the products image has {free} MB free (soft threshold {soft} MB): collecting down to {target} MB
en.removed-temporary: [bazel] removed the leftover capture folder of package {key} in slot {slot}
en.summary: [bazel] removed {packages} packages, {bases} output bases and {temporaries} leftover capture folders of the Bazel sessions
en.summary-dry: [bazel] would remove {packages} packages, {bases} output bases and {temporaries} leftover capture folders of the Bazel sessions
en.collector-busy: [bazel] another Bazel session collector is running; nothing to do here
en.collected-before: [bazel] the Bazel sessions were collected a moment ago by this command
en.pool-would-remove: [bazel] would remove {entries} content pool entries ({megabytes} MB)
en.growth-image: [bazel] every base Bazel server slot is in use but the products image has only {free} MB free (another workspace needs {need} MB): not opening {slot}
en.deduped: [bazel] the identical launcher copies of slot {slot} now share their blocks ({files} files, {megabytes} MB)

en.servers: How many Bazel servers run at once and what each is given: memory share, heap, resident size, cores and growth.
en.waiting: How often a command that waits for a slot polls and reports progress.
en.retention: How many packages a slot keeps and how old a package or an output base may be.
en.stop: How a server is stopped: its pid file and the timeout and polling of the stop.
en.names: The patterns and names of slots, keys, stable packages and state files.
en.leases: The resource names of the slot leases and the most resources one restore holds.
en.pressure: The thresholds of the collection under disk pressure: protected packages, grace, idle time and measuring concurrency.
en.pool: The age after which a pooled package is removed.
en.dedupe: The smallest launcher that is deduplicated and where the stamp of the deduplication lives.
en.limits: The floor of the memory one server is planned with, the longest storage path and how long a sampled spare memory is reused.

de.servers: Wie viele Bazel-Server gleichzeitig laufen und was jeder bekommt: Speicheranteil, Heap, residente Groesse, Kerne und Wachstum.
de.waiting: Wie oft ein Befehl, der auf einen Platz wartet, abfragt und Fortschritt meldet.
de.retention: Wie viele Pakete ein Platz behaelt und wie alt ein Paket oder eine Ausgabebasis sein darf.
de.stop: Wie ein Server gestoppt wird: seine Pid-Datei sowie Zeitlimit und Abfrage des Stoppens.
de.names: Die Muster und Namen von Plaetzen, Schluesseln, stabilen Paketen und Zustandsdateien.
de.leases: Die Ressourcennamen der Platz-Leases und die meisten Ressourcen, die eine Wiederherstellung haelt.
de.pressure: Die Schwellen der Sammlung unter Plattendruck: geschuetzte Pakete, Gnadenfrist, Leerlaufzeit und Messparallelitaet.
de.pool: Das Alter, nach dem ein gepooltes Paket entfernt wird.
de.dedupe: Der kleinste Launcher, der dedupliziert wird, und wo der Stempel der Deduplizierung liegt.
de.limits: Die Untergrenze des Speichers, mit dem ein Server geplant wird, der laengste Speicherpfad und wie lange ein gemessener freier Speicher wiederverwendet wird.
